messages.author: a523f4070ecfcf39
messages.subject: Strange bug with time axes?
parts:
I've been plotting time series lately, and I ran across this problem:

> df<-data.frame(timestamp=as.POSIXct(seq(1,10000*60,60),origin='2011-04-01'),value=runif(10000))
> ggplot(df,aes(timestamp,value))+geom_line()
Error in anyDuplicated.default(breaks) : 
  length 1293868801 is too large for hashing
R allocates a *ton* of memory and locks up for a while before spitting out the error message above.  Another person posted a similar problem on stack overflow: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5325068/r-ggplot-error-too-large-for-hashing

At first I thought it simply had something to do with long timespans, but that's not it.  If I shift the origin to 1970-01-01, things work just fine:

> df<-data.frame(timestamp=as.POSIXct(seq(1,10000*60,60),origin='1970-01-01'),value=runif(10000))
> ggplot(df,aes(timestamp,value))+geom_line()

I've tried playing with different dates and spans, but so far I haven't been able to isolate a better repro case.

I've got the latest plyr as Hadley suggested in the stack overflow thread.  My sessioninfo():

> sessionInfo()
R version 2.12.2 (2011-02-25)
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin9.8.0/x86_64 (64-bit)

locale:
[1] C

attached base packages:
[1] grid      stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

other attached packages:
[1] ggplot2_0.8.9 proto_0.3-8   reshape_0.8.4 plyr_1.5.1   

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] tools_2.12.2

Has anyone else seen this? Any ideas?

-J

messages.author: a523f4070ecfcf39
messages.subject: Re: Strange bug with time axes?

Hmm.. things work as expected if I change the timezone (from my default, PST).

> df<-data.frame(timestamp=as.POSIXct(seq(1,10000*60,60),origin='2011-04-01',tz="UTC"),value=runif(10000))
> ggplot(df,aes(timestamp,value))+geom_line()

Daylight savings time started in March in the US this year, so I don't
think it's got to do with that.

-J

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Strange bug with time axes?
parts:
On 4/18/2011 1:20 PM, Hadley Wickham wrote:
>> Aha! I misunderstood. I've added the output of traceback() to the
>> gist: https://gist.github.com/925852
>>
>> Sorry it's so long, but if I make it shorter the problem vanishes.
>
> Hmmm, that does look like a bug in underlying R code, although it may
> be because something is going wrong in the computation of the
> automatic breaks (I know there are some problems with that code).
>
> Hadley

I did find some underlying R bugs when I went hunting on this (worked on
it yesterday afternoon, but didn't write it up until this morning). See
https://bugs.r-project.org/bugzilla3/show_bug.cgi?id=14559

The original problem needed the last point because that pushed it over
the "5 day" threshold which changed which algorithm was used to find the
breaks. It was still short enough to not have any minor breaks
(implemented using "10 years" as the spacing of the breaks). As it
turned out, the starting date and the 10 year span was just the right
combination to tickle a bug in cut.POSIXt which was DST related
(Something like 10*366 days after the start was on the other side of DST
which as a POSIXlt got manipulated back across DST, or something). I
was able to come up with examples for months and quarters as well, and
submitted a patch. However, being as it is in the base package, I don't
think they update it except at releases.

It is sensitive to the exact starting date/time, so you might be able to
work around it by adjusting the scale a bit (by using expand_limits, say).

As it turns out, you can simplify your example since it is just the
endpoints that matter.

df <-
data.frame(timestamp=as.POSIXct(c(1,600000),origin='2011-04-01'),value=runif(2))
ggplot(df,aes(timestamp,value))+geom_line()


--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
